enrichment.short_title: Whether demolition commenced 1967 outline planning permission
key_facts: Outline planning permission granted in 1967 for demolition of cottages and erection of two bungalows at Crawley.
The owner demolished the cottages between January 1969 and November 1970 but did not build the bungalows.
The claimant sought a lawful development certificate on the basis that development had been begun before the 1974 time limit.
The inspector dismissed the appeal, treating demolition as not development and doubting whether demolition commenced the permitted scheme.
The Secretary of State argued that commencement required a specified operation under section 43(2) and demolition was not construction.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Section 288 application to quash an inspector's decision on a section 192 lawful development certificate appeal.
enrichment.outcome: Application allowed; inspector's decision quashed; permission to appeal granted on the section 43 point.
enrichment.ratio: Where demolition of existing buildings was authorised by outline permission and carried out as part of the permitted scheme, the development had been begun for time-limit purposes notwithstanding that demolition is not a work of construction under section 43(2); an inspector errs in speculating about the landowner's subjective motives when applying Riordan's objective commencement test.

enrichment.short_title: Anti-suit injunction and ISDA non-exclusive jurisdiction clause
key_facts: Royal Bank of Canada and Rabobank disputed a $523.8m Enron-related total return swap governed by English law.
Rabobank commenced proceedings in New York one day before RBC issued English proceedings; claims mirrored each other.
The ISDA Master Agreement contained a non-exclusive English jurisdiction clause permitting parallel foreign proceedings.
RBC sought an injunction restraining Rabobank from pursuing the New York action to judgment, save for discovery.
Andrew Smith J refused the injunction; RBC appealed on the basis that the clause made England the primary forum.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal with permission against refusal of a section 37 anti-suit injunction restraining foreign proceedings.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed; Rabobank permitted to continue the New York proceedings to trial.
enrichment.ratio: A non-exclusive jurisdiction clause that expressly contemplates parallel proceedings in other jurisdictions does not impliedly require trial first in England or prohibit a foreign action from proceeding to judgment; pursuing foreign proceedings to trial is not vexatious or oppressive merely because an English trial is also fixed unless unconscionable conduct is shown.
legal_issues: Effect of a non-exclusive ISDA jurisdiction clause on anti-suit relief
Whether parties impliedly agreed England would have primacy at trial
When parallel foreign proceedings become vexatious or oppressive

enrichment.short_title: Proper respondent for constructive unfair dismissal at community school

key_facts: Mrs Green, deputy head at Victoria Road Primary School, claimed constructive unfair dismissal.

The employment tribunal dismissed the council as respondent, holding the governing body was the sole proper party.
The EAT reinstated the council, treating constructive dismissal as outside the governing body's employment powers.

enrichment.short_title: Section 55 asylum support and Article 3 destitution threshold
key_facts: Mr Zardasht, a 20-year-old Iraqi asylum seeker, applied late for asylum and had section 55 support withdrawn.
He claimed entitlement to support under section 55(5) because refusal would expose him to inhuman or degrading treatment.
He slept rough for about fourteen days in parks and a church with only intermittent access to food.
His evidence lacked detail on food, hygiene, charitable support and inability to fend for himself.
The Secretary of State argued the Pretty threshold was not met and charitable day centres were available.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Judicial review of refusal of asylum support under section 55(5) of the 2002 Act.
enrichment.outcome: Application dismissed; permission to appeal refused; interim relief discharged.
enrichment.ratio: Refusal of section 55 support does not breach Article 3 unless the claimant proves, with detailed evidence, that his condition verges on the severity in Pretty, that charitable support and self-help have been exhausted, and that inhuman or degrading treatment is imminently impending; generic assertions of destitution and homelessness are insufficient.

enrichment.short_title: Letter of credit as condition precedent to FOB laytime
key_facts: Kronos sold Sempra gasoil FOB Constantza under a contract requiring payment by irrevocable letter of credit.
Sempra nominated a vessel that arrived on 28 June 2001 but no letter of credit was opened until 5 or 6 July.
Kronos had no cargo ready until early July because of refinery slippage.
Sempra claimed demurrage from 30 June; Kronos argued laytime could not run before the credit was provided.
The judge held laytime could run independently of the letter of credit condition; Kronos appealed on a preliminary issue.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal on a preliminary issue of law as to when laytime commenced under an FOB sale contract.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; laytime did not run until after the letter of credit was opened, subject to waiver.
enrichment.ratio: Where an FOB contract makes provision of a letter of credit a condition precedent to the seller's duty to perform any part of the loading operation, laytime under incorporated charterparty terms cannot begin to run until that condition is satisfied; the laytime and payment provisions bear on the same subject matter and cannot be treated as independent.

enrichment.short_title: Costs after split outcome in property and business dispute
key_facts: Aujla and Sanghera disputed interests in property called the Mills and payments relating to a transferred business.

enrichment.short_title: Open-cover storage insurance and diverted oil cargoes
key_facts: Glencore held an open facultative/obligatory cargo insurance cover with Alpina relating to oil stored at Fujairah.

Alpina argued storage cover expired after 30 days unless further declared; Glencore contended cover was continuous.

enrichment.short_title: Hello! wedding-photo litigation costs after liability win
key_facts: Michael Douglas, Catherine Zeta-Jones and Hello! Ltd had already litigated breach of confidence over unauthorised wedding photographs.
The Hello! defendants were ordered to pay about £1.05m damages but defeated claims against the Marquesa and on several torts.
Hello! had obtained a false witness statement and procured a misleading letter used in the Court of Appeal injunction appeal.
This hearing determined costs of liability and quantum trials, interest, and whether to set aside the Court of Appeal costs order.
Lindsay J awarded 75% of liability costs and 85% of quantum costs on the standard basis and replaced the CA costs order with no order.
